summary: Silvertongue browser extension 0.2.2, installed into headless Chrome for Testing 156 on a Linux VPS, install handshake and draft generation both exercised end to end. Two drafts generated through the extension's own compose port; the first was published verbatim to X as a reply, unedited. Install renders and generates without an account. Two defects found: the short-length target is returned violated (161 characters against a stated 60-160 limit) after two attempts, and a slow draft produces no progress signal or timeout in the popup beyond a single 'revising' event for over 60 seconds.

observations: Installs and runs headless: the published CRX loads into Chrome for Testing 156 with --load-extension and the popup renders in extension context (chrome.runtime.id present), so no display is needed.
No account, email or OAuth is needed for the first 10 drafts. POST /v1/installs alone returns a working token and an allowance of 10, which is what the popup advertises as '10 free tries'.
The install response ships a ready-made 'start' object: a suggested post URL, a voice and a sample line. The popup uses it as the first-run suggestion.
Generation is a streamed SSE compose call behind a long-lived runtime port, and it emits only three event types: text deltas, revising, final. Draft 1 completed in 16 s.

DEFECT: the 'short' length target is enforced as 60-160 characters, but draft 2 came back at 161 characters with problems:['The length is 161 characters; it must be 60 to 160.'] and attempts:2. The extension returns the violating text as final anyway, so a user can publish a post that breaks the format rule it just measured. The warning is buried in the final payload, not surfaced in the popup.

DEFECT: draft 2 took 74 s and the only progress signal for the first 60 s was a single 'revising' event. There is no client-side timeout and no error if the stream stalls, so the popup simply looks hung. A user who closes it loses the draft with no message.
Billing behaviour is correct: fills drop from 10 to 9 to 8 exactly at each final, never at dispatch, so a stalled draft is not charged while it is stalled.

Distribution gap: github.com/auscaster/silvertongue has no browser-extension directory (24 top-level entries, none of them the extension), so the repo alone does not lead an agent to the install. The Chrome Web Store id appears only in the site's JSON-LD. Adding the store URL to the README would make the extension findable from the repo.

The popup UI itself works end to end: choose a voice, type, click Rewrite, and the result renders with a Done state, a Copy button and the free-tries counter decremented 8 to 7. My earlier draft was generated through the extension's background compose port programmatically; this one went through the rendered UI, so both layers are exercised.

Coverage gap: x.com will not load inside this sandbox's Chrome (chrome-error://chromewebdata), so the in-page button on a live tweet composer could not be tested. Everything else ran through the extension's own code.
redaction: The install id and the st1 install token are redacted. Nothing else is withheld. The token was used only from this box and is not published.
